kurz: Rub meat with salt and leave it uncovered in the fridge. It gets seasoned all the way through, juicier, and the surface dries for a better crust.
bild_im_kopf: Like steeping tea: in the first minutes almost nothing happens; only with time does it reach everywhere.
was_passiert: First the [[salz|salt]] draws juice to the surface. The salt dissolves in it, and the salty solution slowly moves back into the meat. There it loosens proteins so the meat holds more water as it cooks. Uncovered in the fridge, the surface dries at the same time.
warum_wichtig: Juicier, evenly seasoned and with a dry surface for the crust: three benefits from one step.
faustregeln: After an hour the salt is only on the outside: either salt right before cooking or properly far ahead.
schritte: Salt evenly all over, about 1 % of the meat's weight (as a guide).
Put it uncovered on a rack in the fridge.
Steaks at least overnight, poultry and roasts 24–48 hours.
Do not rinse before cooking, just pat dry.
